clusters.headline_hint: Crypto exchange Binance targeted in record $6.3 billion cyber heist linked to North Korea

claims.text: Binance froze around half of the stolen funds after $6.3 billion was accessed in a cyber heist.
Binance secured $3 billion of its stolen digital assets, while remaining funds were held by unidentified hackers.
Analytics firms linked the Binance hack to a North Korean hacking unit.
The Binance cyber heist eclipsed a $1.5 billion hack on the Bybit exchange in 2025.
The US Secret Service stated it was working around the clock to identify, freeze, trace, and recover stolen Binance funds.
Binance co-CEO Richard Teng stated that hackers used a self-destruct mechanism that destroyed tooling and traces as they went.
Binance set aside more than $6.34 billion in company funds to cover the stolen assets.
The price of Bitcoin fell 5% to $76,800 in Friday afternoon trading in New York following news of the Binance hack.
Binance was founded in China in 2017 and is estimated to have over 300 million registered users worldwide.
Experts, including TRM Labs, attributed the $6.3 billion Binance cryptocurrency theft to TraderTraitor, an elite North Korean hacking unit also known as the Lazarus Group.
A UN panel of experts reported in spring 2024 that it was reviewing 58 suspected North Korean cyber-attacks on cryptocurrency companies between 2017 and 2023 worth $3 billion.
Cryptocurrency theft is estimated to generate half of North Korea's foreign currency income.
In February 2016, North Korean hackers attempted to illicitly move $951 million from Bangladesh Bank's account at the Federal Reserve Bank of New York, ultimately stealing $81 million.
Blockchain intelligence firm TRM reported that an attacker moved approximately $6.36 billion out of Binance wallets on ten blockchains, mostly within 20 minutes.
Chainalysis co-founder and CEO Jonathan Levin stated on X that the Binance hack was likely done by the DPRK group TraderTraitor.
Former Binance CEO Changpeng Zhao was pardoned by US President Donald Trump in 2025 after pleading guilty in 2023 to failing to prevent money laundering on the platform.
NyxLab CEO Kok Tin Gan stated the attack appeared to involve one signature granting a never-expiring, full-access token to a Binance hot wallet.

clusters.headline_hint: Israeli general election ends in deadlock as Benjamin Netanyahu's bloc falls short of majority

claims.text: Benjamin Netanyahu accused Palestinian Israeli parties of stealing the Israeli election and accepting funding from Qatar.
Israel's Electoral Commission found no evidence of fraud regarding Palestinian Israeli parties, and Qatar denied involvement.
Israeli security agency Shin Bet investigated suspicions regarding whether Arab-led parties received illegal foreign funding from Qatar and Turkey.
The Arab party lists The Joint List and Ra'am won a record 19 seats in the 120-seat Knesset following high turnout among Arab voters.
Benjamin Netanyahu's bloc won 53 seats in the Israeli parliamentary election, while Gadi Eisenkot's rival bloc secured 48 seats.
Acting Central Elections Committee Director General Dean Livne stated there was no basis for allegations of systematic violations of election integrity.
Arab Israelis make up approximately one-fifth of Israel's population.
German Foreign Ministry spokesperson Martin Giese stated Germany will do everything possible to work well with any future Israeli government.
German Development Minister Reem Alabali Radovan called for an immediate stop to radical Israeli settler violence in the occupied West Bank and East Jerusalem.
Around 3,000 Palestinians were driven from their homes during a major Israeli military operation near Hebron following the reported killing of two Israeli soldiers.
Benjamin Netanyahu's Likud party won 27 seats, remaining the largest party in the Knesset, but his right-wing coalition won 53 seats, short of the 61 needed for a majority.
In Israel, a candidate given the mandate to form a government has 28 days to secure support from at least 61 lawmakers, with a possible extension of up to 14 days.
US President Donald Trump endorsed Benjamin Netanyahu prior to the Israeli election.

clusters.headline_hint: Civilians evacuated from Russian-occupied Ukrainian town of Oleshky during rare ceasefire

claims.text: Hundreds of residents were evacuated from the Russian-occupied city of Oleshky during a four-hour window as part of a humanitarian ceasefire.
The localized humanitarian ceasefire in Oleshky was brokered by US First Lady Melania Trump.
Ukrainian negotiator David Arakhamia stated that evacuated residents of Oleshky traveled to Anapa in Russia, from where they would fly to Belarus and travel by bus to Ukraine.
Russia's human rights ombudsman Yana Lantratova stated that 25 buses and nine ambulances were deployed for the Oleshky evacuations.
The population of Oleshky declined from a pre-war total of 24,000 to approximately 2,000.
A Russian drone strike on a train station in the Ukrainian city of Dnipro killed at least 13 people on Thursday.
The localized ceasefire allowed roads leading out of Oleshky to be de-mined to make evacuations possible.
The Kremlin described the Oleshky ceasefire as a special case that was difficult to extrapolate to broader peace negotiations.
Oleshky was captured by Russian forces in February 2022 and suffered severe flooding following the destruction of the Kakhovka dam in June 2023.
Ukrainian human rights ombudsman Dmytro Lubinets stated this was the first time since 2022 that a ceasefire across such an extensive frontline stretch was maintained for a significant duration.

clusters.headline_hint: Polish police deployed to Constitutional Tribunal following suspension of chief judge

claims.text: Polish police entered the Constitutional Tribunal premises in Warsaw after demonstrators gathered outside and threw objects at officers.
Constitutional Tribunal head Bogdan Swieczkowski was suspended after using his authority to block judges elected by the parliamentary majority from performing court duties.
Justice Minister Waldemar Zurek requested that legal immunity be lifted for Bogdan Swieczkowski and his deputy so they could face criminal charges.
Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk stated on X that restoring the rule of law after years of PiS lawlessness is a difficult, sometimes painful process requiring decisive action.
Polish President Karol Nawrocki turned his plane around while en route to Senegal, stating the president must be in Poland during the court crisis.
Judge Anna Korwin-Piotrowska was placed in charge of the Constitutional Tribunal following Swieczkowski's suspension.
The Constitutional Court published a statement on social media calling the actions against its top judges a coup d'etat and insisting they remain legally appointed.
President Karol Nawrocki has refused to swear in five Constitutional Court judges elected by parliament since March.
The Venice Commission advised President Nawrocki earlier in October to swear in the parliament-elected judges to allow them to sit on the bench.
Supporters of the opposition Law and Justice party gathered outside the Constitutional Tribunal chanting Tusk traitor and praying.

clusters.headline_hint: Independent Russian newspaper Novaya Gazeta announces closure amid state pressure

claims.text: Independent Russian newspaper Novaya Gazeta announced its closure after being evicted from its office of 30 years and blocked from receiving reader donations.
Novaya Gazeta co-founder Dmitry Muratov won the Nobel Peace Prize in 2021 and was designated a foreign agent by Russian authorities in 2023.
Six Novaya Gazeta journalists have been killed over the years, including Anna Politkovskaya who was shot dead in October 2006.
Novaya Gazeta investigative journalist Oleg Roldugin was arrested earlier in 2026 and charged with unlawful access to computerized information.
Novaya Gazeta editor-in-chief Sergei Sokolov was questioned by police and had his home searched in connection with Roldugin's case.
Editor-in-chief Sergei Sokolov wrote on Novaya Gazeta's website that the newspaper found itself in a kill zone after nearly five years of working while encircled by security services.
Following Russia's 2022 invasion of Ukraine, Novaya Gazeta published blank white spaces in print to indicate censored text.
Dmitry Muratov was doused with red paint while on a train in April 2022, causing damage to his eyesight.
Exiled Novaya Gazeta journalists set up Novaya Gazeta Europe, while Muratov's team in Russia printed magazines with runs of 999 copies to bypass official licensing requirements.
Landlords informed Novaya Gazeta staff that they must vacate their central Moscow office newsroom by November 9.

clusters.headline_hint: Six killed as helicopter carrying pilgrims crashes near Joshimath in Uttarakhand

claims.text: Six people were killed after a helicopter crashed near Joshimath in Uttarakhand's Chamoli district on Friday.
The Aircraft Accident Investigation Bureau recommended that pilots complete 50 hours of supervised hill flying before operating alone in the Kedarnath valley.
The Aircraft Accident Investigation Bureau recorded eight accidents and one serious incident in the Char Dham sector between 2015 and 2025.
The civil aviation ministry introduced safety measures for the 2026 pilgrimage season, including air traffic control units at Sahastradhara in Dehradun and Sersi in Rudraprayag.
Ministry of Civil Aviation data presented in the Rajya Sabha showed six helicopter accidents during the Char Dham Yatra between 2021 and June 2025.
On May 8, 2025, an Aero Trans Services Bell 407 crashed near Gangnani in Uttarkashi after its main rotor struck a fibre-optic cable, killing six people.
On June 15, 2025, an Aryan Aviation Bell 407 crashed near Gaurikund while flying from Kedarnath to Guptkashi, killing all seven people on board.
On October 18, 2022, an Aryan Aviation Bell 407 crashed into a mountain ridge near Garud Chatti, killing all seven people on board.
The helicopter involved in Friday's crash near Joshimath was operated by Trans Bharat.
The Uttarakhand state government grounded the entire Trans Bharat fleet following the Friday helicopter crash.
On October 24, 2026, a Trans Bharat helicopter carrying five pilgrims made an emergency landing at Baurari stadium.
On May 20, 2026, a Trans Bharat Bell 407 carrying seven people struck a high-tension power line during an emergency landing in Tehri Garhwal, leaving no occupants injured.
Five pilgrims and one pilot died when their helicopter crashed near Joshimath on Friday.
The helicopter lost contact after taking off from the Hindu pilgrimage site of Badrinath on Friday afternoon.
India's weather department had issued an orange alert for the region before the crash, warning of thunderstorms, hail, and strong winds.
Uttarakhand Chief Minister Pushkar Singh Dhami stated that the helicopter came down near a village close to Joshimath in Chamoli district.
The civil helicopter operated by Trans Bharat Aviation crashed in the Hathi Parvat area of Chamoli district while flying from Badrinath to Sahastradhara helipad in Dehradun.
The helicopter took off from Badrinath at 1:14 pm on Friday carrying six people before going missing.
The deceased pilot was identified as Captain Himanshu, and the five deceased passengers were identified as Prathapa, Arun, Shankar Gowda, Sudheer K, and HS Natraja.
The five passengers who died in the Friday helicopter crash were from Bengaluru.

clusters.headline_hint: ISRO successfully launches next-generation navigation satellite NVS-03 to bolster NavIC system

claims.text: ISRO successfully launched the NVS-03 satellite aboard the GSLV-F18 rocket from the Satish Dhawan Space Centre in Sriharikota on Friday, October 30, 2026.
The GSLV-F18 rocket placed the 2,250 kg NVS-03 satellite into geosynchronous transfer orbit 18 minutes after liftoff.
ISRO Chairman Dr. V. Narayanan stated that the success of the NVS-03 mission restored the NavIC constellation to its minimum operational configuration of four satellites.
The last functioning atomic clock aboard the IRNSS-1F satellite stopped working on March 13, 2026, leaving only three operational satellites in the NavIC constellation.
The GSLV-F18 mission was accomplished with a turnaround time of 56 days following the GSLV-F17 mission.
The NVS-03 satellite carries an indigenously manufactured atomic clock alongside imported atomic clocks.
India's armed forces rely on foreign navigation systems including US GPS and Russian GLONASS when NavIC has fewer than four operational satellites.
NavIC was originally designed with a constellation of seven satellites placed in geostationary and geosynchronous orbits.
The replacement satellite NVS-02 failed to reach its intended orbit on January 29, 2025, due to a pyro valve signal loss in its engine.
The NVS-03 satellite transmits signals in the L1, L5, and S bands, making NavIC compatible with modern civilian smartphone chipsets.
In June 2025, the Indian government announced plans to replace US GPS with five atomic clocks located across India to maintain Indian Standard Time.
The 51.7-metre-tall GSLV Mk II rocket lifted off from the Second Launch Pad at Sriharikota at 11:51 pm IST on October 30, 2026.
ISRO kept specific valves open before launch to prevent a recurrence of the technical issue that affected NVS-02.

clusters.headline_hint: Oil tanker with 27 Indian seafarers struck in Strait of Hormuz attack

claims.text: December Brent crude futures rose $2.76, or 2.4 percent, to settle at $117.64 a barrel on Friday.
The UK Maritime Trade Operations reported that a tanker in the Strait of Hormuz was struck on Friday by explosive devices attached by a small boat.
Yemen's Houthi militants claimed attacks on several Saudi Arabian sites, including the Ras Tanura and Rabigh oil refineries and the Abqaiq production facility.
An armed group closed a valve on Libya's Hamada crude oil pipeline on Friday, stopping a flow of approximately 15,000 barrels per day.
The Omani Maritime Security Centre evacuated 25 crew members from the burning Panamanian-flagged oil tanker RITI in the Strait of Hormuz on Friday.
Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps stated that three oil tankers were stopped after attempting to cross the Strait of Hormuz through unauthorised routes.
US Central Command chief Brad Cooper stated on Friday that internationally recognised primary transit routes in the Strait of Hormuz had been cleared of Iranian sea mines.
External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar raised concerns about attacks on civilian shipping and seafarers during the G20 foreign ministers' meeting on Friday.
The Panama-flagged oil tanker MT Louise 1, carrying 27 Indian seafarers, was targeted with limpet mines in the Strait of Hormuz.
Union Minister Sarbananda Sonowal confirmed that all 29 Indian seafarers across MT Arzanah and MT Louise 1 were safe following attacks in the Strait of Hormuz.
The October 30 limpet mine attack on MT Louise 1 damaged its engine room and temporarily disabled the vessel before the onboard fire was controlled.
On October 29, the Liberia-flagged MT Arzanah, carrying two Indian nationals, was targeted in a projectile attack in the Strait of Hormuz.
Limpet mines are small explosive devices attached to a ship's hull using magnets to damage critical machinery without necessarily sinking the vessel.
